threads.thread_goal: Align on current workflow, main pain points and pilot scope for one aisle.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Store Backroom-to-Shelf Replenishment Optimisation Pilot for one aisle.
To get started, can each of you describe how the backroom-to-shelf flow works today from your side, step by step? I will consolidate this into the workflow map for T1 and update A1.
Also, we need to pick one aisle and product categories for the pilot, and agree when we start within the 21-day window.
Please share:
- Which aisle you think is a good candidate and why
- Where you see delays, safety issues or stock accuracy problems
- Any shift-specific quirks (day vs evening)
Once we have that, I will draft the first version of the Shift Task Allocation and Rotation Plan (A6, T6).

From my side on the loading and moving:
- We unload the truck at the back dock, then I sort pallets roughly by aisle, but not always by product type.
- I usually stack heavier boxes at the bottom on the trolley, but sometimes we mix chilled with ambient if space is tight.
- I push trolleys to the aisle when there is space, but often the aisle is busy with customers or cleaning.
Pain points:
- We get blocked in the corridor near the chiller when cleaning is going on.
- Some pallets are overloaded and it is hard to see over them.
For the pilot aisle, I would suggest the dairy and chilled drinks aisle, because that is where I see the most back-and-forth trips.

On shelf filling:
- For dairy and chilled drinks, I usually pull the trolley from the back corridor, park it at the end of the aisle, then work section by section.
- I try to rotate stock, but when the trolley is mixed it is hard to find the oldest dates quickly.
- Labels and prices: I change labels when I notice a mismatch, but there is no fixed moment in the routine.
Pain points:
- Trolleys sometimes arrive half full of unrelated items, so I waste time sorting.
- In the evening shift, we often get last-minute pallets that we cannot finish before closing.
I agree dairy and chilled drinks could be a good pilot aisle, but we need to be careful with food safety and shelf life checks.

From the office side:
- I receive the delivery paperwork, check against the system, and then note which pallets go to which aisles.
- Right now, the mapping from pallets to aisles is quite rough, and we do not log where delays happen.
- Stock counts for the aisle are done once a day, but not always at the same time.
Pain points:
- When replenishment is late, the system still shows stock available, so we get customer complaints.
- We do not have a clear view of which shift caused a delay.
For T1, I will map the current steps from truck unloading to shelf filling for the dairy and chilled drinks aisle, using your inputs. That will become the updated A1.
On pilot scope, I suggest we include all dairy and chilled drinks products in that aisle, both branded and own label, so we see enough volume but still keep it manageable.

Adding what I see from the desk:
- I log delivery times and sometimes note if a pallet is damaged, but I do not always record which aisle it was for.
- For the dairy aisle, I usually get calls from the floor when there are gaps, then I check the system and confirm stock is in the back.
- There is no standard way to record these exceptions yet.
I can help fill out forms and keep the workflow doc updated once we agree the exact steps for T1.

Thanks for the detail on loading and movement.
Follow-up questions:
- When you say pallets are overloaded, is that mainly on dairy and chilled drinks, or across all categories?
- How often do you mix chilled with ambient on the same trolley for that aisle?
This will help when we design the standard sequence later for T2 and link it to the shift plan in A6.

Overloaded pallets happen mostly on dairy and chilled drinks, especially on the first delivery of the week.
Mixing chilled with ambient on the same trolley for that aisle happens maybe half the time, usually when we are short on trolleys or in a rush.
If we fix the loading sequence in T2, I think we can keep chilled together and avoid stacking too high.

On the shelf side, your point about mixed trolleys is important.
For the current workflow map in A1, I will note that sorting is happening at the aisle instead of in the backroom.
Can you confirm roughly how long it takes you to fill the full dairy and chilled drinks aisle on a normal delivery, and how that changes on evening shifts?

On a normal morning delivery, filling the full dairy and chilled drinks aisle takes about 90 minutes if the trolley is well organised.
If the trolley is mixed and I have to sort a lot, it can go up to 2 hours.
On evening shifts, it is similar, but we lose time when customers are in the way and when we get late pallets close to closing time.

I can support with T6 once T1 and A1 are drafted.
My idea is to:
- Split the dairy and chilled drinks aisle into clear sections for each shift.
- Assign movers and shelf fillers per section and time slot, so we avoid everyone arriving at once.
- Add a simple rotation so the same person is not always on the heaviest section.
I will sketch a first version of A6 after we lock the pilot aisle and start date.

So far, everyone seems aligned on using the dairy and chilled drinks aisle as the pilot area, covering all products in that aisle.
Unless there are strong objections, I suggest we confirm that as our pilot scope for D1.
On timing: given the 21-day limit, I propose we start next Monday, run the pilot for the full 21 days, and do a mid-pilot review at the end of week one.
Does that work for day and evening shifts?

Starting next Monday works for me.
For evenings, I suggest we avoid testing big changes on Friday and Saturday nights, as those are busier.
We can still follow the new routine, but maybe keep some flexibility those days.
I am fine confirming the dairy and chilled drinks aisle as the pilot area.

Next Monday start is ok from my side.
For the first week, it would help if we can keep the same movers on the dairy and chilled drinks aisle so we get used to the new flow.
I agree with using that aisle for the pilot.

I can adjust the paperwork and any forms from next Monday.
I will also start a simple log for that aisle so we can capture delays and issues until T9 is ready.
No objections on the aisle choice or the 21-day window.

From the office side, starting next Monday and running the full 21 days is fine.
I will inform the store operations manager and inventory controller so they know the dairy and chilled drinks aisle is our pilot area.
We can schedule the mid-pilot review at the end of next week and use A1 and A6 to show the before and after.

Summarising this thread so far:
- Pilot aisle: dairy and chilled drinks, full aisle, all products (D1 confirmed).
- Pilot timing: start next Monday, run for 21 days, with a mid-pilot review at the end of week one (D2 confirmed).
Next steps from here:
- I will complete the current workflow map for T1 and update A1.
- Together with 331660, I will draft the first version of A6 for T6, based on your inputs on shifts and pain points.
We will share both in the next thread before we lock the new routines.

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate the new loading, movement and shelf routines.

messages.text:
As agreed, here is the first draft of the new loading and movement sequence and the shelf replenishment routine for the dairy and chilled drinks aisle.
Loading and movement (draft A2, from T2):
- Separate pallets by aisle and by temperature zone in the backroom.
- Build trolleys so chilled dairy and chilled drinks are together, heavier items at the bottom, lighter on top, within equipment capacity.
- Limit trolley height so movers can see over the load.
- Move trolleys to the aisle in smaller batches to avoid blocking.
Shelf replenishment routine (draft A4, from T4):
- Start with checking dates and rotating stock, then fill from back to front.
- Check labels and prices as you go, correcting any mismatches.
- Keep the aisle clear for customers and cleaning.
Please review and comment. We need to agree on the final versions for D3 and D4 before Monday.

On the loading side, this looks doable.
Questions:
- For separating pallets by temperature zone, do we have enough space in the backroom to keep chilled dairy and chilled drinks apart from ambient?
- For trolley height, can we set a simple rule, like not higher than my shoulders, so it is easy to follow?
I like the idea of smaller batches to avoid blocking, but we will need to coordinate with cleaning for T10 so we do not clash in the corridor.

On the shelf routine:
- Starting with date checks and rotation is good, but we should be clear on how to handle short-dated items we cannot fit on the shelf.
- For labels and prices, can we add a step to check the promo section separately? That is where I see most mismatches.
- We should also define how many sections we aim to complete before we move the trolley, so we do not leave it blocking the aisle.
Overall, the structure in A4 makes sense to me.

On space in the backroom: we cannot change the layout, but we can mark zones on the floor for chilled dairy and chilled drinks.
For trolley height, I like the simple rule you suggested. We can write it into A2 as 'do not stack higher than shoulder level of the mover using the trolley'.
On T10, I will speak with the cleaning and maintenance coordinator so we can align cleaning times with the new movement sequence and avoid blocked aisles.

For the shelf routine, I can help by preparing a simple printed version of A4 that shelf fillers can keep on the trolley.
I just need the final steps confirmed for T4.
Also, should we add a note about where to put empty packaging and waste so it does not block the aisle?

Good points on short-dated items and promos.
Proposal to update A4:
- After date checks, if we find short-dated items that do not fit on the shelf, we place them in a clearly marked short-date section in the chiller and inform the duty manager.
- Add a specific step to check promo labels and prices at the end of each section.
- Define that the trolley should be parked at the end of the aisle or in a bay that does not block customers while we work on a section.
Would that cover your concerns for T4?

Yes, that works for me.
One more detail: can we specify that we always pull older stock forward before adding new, even if it means taking a bit longer on busy days?
That will help with food safety and reduce waste.

Agreed. I will add a clear line in A4 that we always pull older stock forward before placing new items, even on busy days, unless a manager explicitly instructs otherwise.
That will also link nicely with the safety and hygiene checklist in A3 later.

The floor markings in the backroom will help.
For the loading sequence in A2, can we also say:
- Put the heaviest crates at the bottom, then medium, then light.
- Keep liquids low so they do not crush softer items.
I want to be sure we stay within the lifting equipment capacity and avoid strain.

Yes, we can add those rules into A2.
I will also include a reminder to check the trolley and pallet capacity labels before loading, so we do not exceed limits.
Once we finalise the text, we should run T7 on two delivery days to test the new sequence and log any issues.

On your earlier question about space: I checked the backroom layout.
We can create two marked zones for chilled dairy and chilled drinks without moving any fixed structures.
We will need to keep those zones clear of other stock, so I will add that as a note in A2.
If we see that it is not working during T7, we can adjust.

On empty packaging and waste, I suggest we:
- Flatten cardboard and place it on the bottom of the trolley once a section is done.
- Put plastic wrap and small waste in a bag attached to the trolley.
- Take all waste back to the backroom at the end of the aisle before moving to the next section.
We can add this to A4 so it is part of the routine.

Good addition. I will include the waste handling steps in A4.
We should also make sure T10 reflects that cleaning will not start in the aisle until waste is cleared and trolleys are parked in the agreed spots.

Based on the feedback, I have updated A2 and A4 with:
- Clear loading rules on weight distribution, trolley height and temperature zones.
- Movement in smaller batches with marked backroom zones and agreed parking spots.
- Shelf routine steps for rotation, short-dated items, promo checks, waste handling and keeping aisles clear.
Unless there are any last-minute concerns today, I propose we approve these as the standard loading and movement sequence and shelf replenishment routine for the pilot (D3 and D4), and use them from Monday.
We will still be able to fine-tune after the first week if needed.

I am ok with the updated A2.
The rules are clear enough for loading and moving, and I can follow them from Monday.
Happy to confirm for the pilot.

I am comfortable with the updated A4.
The steps for rotation, promos and waste are clear, and I can start using this routine on Monday.
Ok to confirm it for the pilot.

From the office side, I support approving A2 and A4 as our standard for the pilot.
I will make sure the store operations manager and health and safety officer see the final versions before Monday.
We can then schedule T7 and T8 in the shift plan so we know exactly which days we are testing what.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in safety, hygiene and incident logging practices for the pilot.

messages.text:
Sharing the draft safety and hygiene checklist and the incident and exception log for the pilot.
Safety and hygiene checklist (draft A3, from T3 and linked to T12):
- Check PPE and safe lifting posture before starting.
- Confirm trolley and pallet loads are within capacity and not stacked above shoulder height.
- For dairy and chilled drinks, check temperatures, packaging integrity and dates before filling.
- Ensure rotation is done correctly and short-dated items are handled as agreed.
Incident and exception log (draft A7, from T9):
- Simple form to record damaged goods, missing items, unsafe situations, delays and any hygiene issues.
- Fields: date, time, aisle, product, description, who reported, immediate action.
Please review and comment. We need to confirm the final checklist (D5) and agree when and how to fill in the log (D6) before the pilot starts.

On the checklist for movers:
- I like the reminder about trolley capacity and height.
- Could we add a quick step to check the floor for spills or obstacles before moving a loaded trolley?
For the incident log, I am ok filling it in, but I will need a clear example of what counts as an incident versus something we just fix on the spot.

From the shelf side:
- The checklist items on rotation and dates look good.
- I suggest we add a line to check that chilled doors close properly and are not blocked by trolleys or boxes.
On the incident log, I think we should log any case where we have to remove products from sale due to date or temperature issues, not just physical damage.

Good point on spills and obstacles.
I will add a step in A3 for movers to check the floor and clear any hazards before moving a loaded trolley.
On what counts as an incident in A7, my suggestion:
- Log anything that could affect safety, product quality or customer experience, even if you fix it.
- Examples: near misses with trolleys, repeated delays, products found out of temperature, damaged packaging, or missing items.
We can include a short example list at the top of the form.

I can help by keeping the A7 log file up to date.
Question on T9: who should be responsible for entering the incidents, the person who sees it or the office?
Maybe we can say that movers and shelf fillers note the basics on paper during the shift, and I enter them into A7 at the end of the day.

For T9 and D6, I like the split you suggest.
Proposal:
- Whoever spots the incident (mover or shelf filler) fills a short paper slip during the shift.
- At the end of the day, office staff consolidate all slips into the digital A7 log.
- If there is a serious safety or hygiene issue, the person who spots it must also call the duty manager immediately, not wait for the log.
We can also link this to T12 so the health and safety officer can review non-compliance cases.

That process works for me.
For timing, should we say that we fill the paper slip as soon as we can after the incident, ideally within the same hour, so we do not forget details?

I am ok with filling a paper slip when something happens.
It would help to have the slips stored near the back door so we can grab them quickly.
On the checklist A3, can we also remind movers to keep hands clear of pinch points when turning trolleys in tight spaces?

I will add the door check into A3: confirm chilled doors close fully and are not blocked by stock or trolleys.
On logging products removed from sale, we can add a specific tick box in A7 for 'removed from sale due to date or temperature'.
That will make it easier to summarise later for T11.

I can take responsibility for entering all slips into A7 at the end of each day during the pilot.
I will also prepare three example incidents in the log so everyone can see how to fill it, as part of T9.

I have now incorporated your feedback into A3 and A7:
- Added checks for spills, obstacles, pinch points and chilled doors.
- Clarified rotation, short-dated handling and temperature checks.
- Defined that incidents are logged on paper slips during the shift and consolidated into A7 daily, with urgent issues escalated immediately.
Unless there are objections, I suggest we confirm this version of the safety and hygiene checklist as final for the pilot (D5) and lock the incident logging process as described (D6).

I am happy with the updated A3 and A7.
The steps are clear and fit into the normal flow of the shift.
Ok to confirm them for the pilot.

No objections from me.
The checklist A3 covers what I need to remember before moving loads, and the log process is simple enough.
Ok to go ahead for the pilot.

I will now share A3 and A7 with the health and safety officer for confirmation that they meet requirements under T12.
Assuming they are comfortable, we can brief the team on the first day of the pilot and start using both tools from day one.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate daily execution, tracking and quick fixes during the pilot.

messages.text:
Pilot day 1 for the dairy and chilled drinks aisle.
For this thread, let us use it as our daily async check-in at shift change.
Please share:
- What you completed for your part of the new sequence or routine (T7, T8, T10).
- Any issues, incidents or delays (with a note if you logged them in A7).
- Plan for the next shift.
Also, we need to decide how often we update the stock accuracy and shelf condition tracking sheet A5 and share a quick status here (D7).

Morning shift update from the backroom and movement side:
- Used the new loading sequence from A2 for the first dairy and chilled drinks delivery (T7).
- Kept trolley height below shoulder level and separated chilled dairy from chilled drinks.
- Marked the floor zones and used them as planned.
Issues:
- One small spill near the chiller, cleaned immediately and noted on a paper slip for A7.
Plan for next shift:
- Keep using the same sequence on the second delivery today and watch for any bottlenecks in the corridor.

Morning shelf filling update (T8):
- Followed the new A4 routine for the full dairy and chilled drinks aisle.
- Checked dates and rotated stock, moved short-dated items to the marked section.
- Checked promo labels and prices; found two mismatches and corrected them.
- Cleared waste as per the new steps.
No major incidents, just one case of slightly damaged packaging that I removed from sale and logged on a slip for A7.
For the tracking sheet A5, I filled in the morning counts and noted shelf gaps and mispriced items.

Office update:
- Collected the incident slips from the morning and entered them into A7.
- Updated A5 with the morning stock counts and shelf condition notes from 321832.
Question for D7: do we want to update A5 once per day or twice (morning and evening)?
From my side, twice a day is manageable during the pilot.

I recommend we update A5 twice a day during the pilot: once after the main morning fill and once after the main evening fill.
That will give us a better view of gaps and mispricing across shifts.
For D7, we could also agree that each shift posts a short status in this thread when they complete their update, so we keep a running log.

Twice-daily updates to A5 plus a short status here sounds right for D7.
Proposal:
- Morning shift: update A5 after the main fill and post a quick summary.
- Evening shift: do the same after their main fill.
- Office: check both entries and make sure any incidents in A7 are linked.
If everyone is ok, we will treat this as our standard for the pilot.

Works for me.
I can give a short note here after I finish the loading and movement for each main delivery, and mention if anything might affect the counts in A5.

I am fine with updating A5 after each main fill and posting a quick status.
For evenings, I will also note if we leave any sections unfinished so the morning shift knows where to pick up.

Ok for me as well.
I will check A5 after each update and make sure any related incidents are in A7.
If I see missing entries, I will ping the shift that should have filled them.

End of day 1 summary:
- T7: new loading and movement sequence used on both deliveries, one minor spill incident logged in A7.
- T8: new shelf routine followed for the full aisle, two price mismatches corrected, one damaged pack removed from sale and logged.
- T10: cleaning was mostly aligned, but there was a short overlap in the corridor after the second delivery; we will adjust the cleaning slot by 15 minutes tomorrow.
A5 has morning and evening entries now, and we have three incidents recorded in A7.
Please keep using this thread for daily updates for the rest of the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on next steps and improvements.

messages.text:
We have reached the end of the 21-day pilot for the dairy and chilled drinks aisle.
I have prepared a draft summary of the tracking data and incidents in A8, based on A5 and A7, as part of T11.
Headline observations:
- Shelf gaps reduced by around one third compared to the first week.
- Price mismatches dropped steadily after the first few days.
- Most incidents in A7 were minor spills, short-dated items and a few delays due to cleaning overlaps.
In this thread, let us:
- Share your view on what worked well and what did not.
- Propose which process changes we should keep.
- Decide whether to extend the process to more aisles and under what conditions (D8).

From the mover side:
What worked well:
- The floor markings and trolley height rule in A2 made it easier to load safely.
- Separating chilled dairy and chilled drinks reduced confusion at the aisle.
- Once cleaning times were adjusted under T10, we had fewer blocked corridors.
What did not work so well:
- On very busy delivery days, keeping loads small meant more trips, and I felt rushed.
I would keep the loading rules and floor markings if we extend to other aisles, but we might need to review how many trolleys we have available.

From the shelf side:
What worked well:
- The A4 routine helped me keep a consistent order: dates, rotation, fill, labels, waste.
- Short-dated items were easier to manage with the dedicated section.
- Customers seemed to notice fewer gaps, especially in the evenings.
What did not work so well:
- On some nights, we did not have enough time to complete the full routine for the whole aisle, so a few sections were rushed.
If we extend to more aisles, I would keep the routine but make sure the shift plan in A6 gives enough time per section.

From the office side:
- A5 was filled twice a day most days; when it was complete, it was easy to see patterns in gaps and mispricing.
- A7 now has more than the three sample incidents required by T9, and we can see that spills and short-dated items were the main themes.
- Entering incidents daily took some time, but it helped us catch repeated issues.
If we extend, I would keep A5 and A7 as they are, but maybe simplify the incident description field so it is quicker to fill.

Looking at A8 and the data from A5 and A7:
Successes:
- Clear reduction in shelf gaps and price errors.
- Fewer last-minute rushes in the aisle once A6 and T10 were tuned.
- Safety and hygiene incidents stayed low and were mostly minor.
Issues:
- Some days, evening updates to A5 were missing or late.
- A few incidents were not logged until the next day.
For D8, my suggestion is:
- We keep the new loading sequence, shelf routine, checklist and logging process as our standard for the dairy and chilled drinks aisle.
- We extend the pilot approach to one more chilled aisle, but only after we adjust the shift plan in A6 and confirm we have enough trolleys and time per section.

I support that direction for D8.
To make it concrete:
- For the dairy and chilled drinks aisle, we keep using A2, A4, A3, A5, A6 and A7 as our standard.
- For the next aisle, we run a shorter pilot using the same tools, but we first update A6 to reflect the extra workload and check trolley availability.
We will also capture three specific improvement proposals in A8 as part of T11: simplifying the incident description, reinforcing evening updates to A5, and reviewing trolley numbers.

I am ok with keeping the new process on the dairy and chilled drinks aisle and trying it on another chilled aisle.
Before we extend, I would like us to confirm how many trolleys we can dedicate to chilled, so we do not end up overloading again.

I agree with keeping the routine on the current aisle.
For the next aisle, we should make sure the shift plan in A6 gives enough time for rotation and label checks, especially in the evenings.
If that is in place, I am comfortable extending.

From my side, I am fine with extending to another aisle as long as we keep the incident log A7 manageable.
If we simplify the description field and keep the twice-daily A5 updates, I can handle the extra entries.

To close this out:
- We confirm that the new process remains in place for the dairy and chilled drinks aisle.
- We agree to extend the approach to one additional chilled aisle, after updating A6 and checking trolley availability (D8 confirmed).
Next steps:
- I will update A6 with the new allocation and rotation for both aisles.
- 37492 will finalise A8 with the three improvement proposals under T11.
- We will share the updated plan with the store operations manager and health and safety officer before starting the second aisle.
